thread:
julian: quick heads-up — on the zeta-2A int8 canary with batching=auto + prefix KV cache we see ~1% of requests where the function invocation returns a valid JSON object then a few random non-utf8-ish bytes after the closing brace. appears only when batch_size > 1 and streaming is enabled.

sara: ugh. any sample outputs?

julian: yes, pasted below (redacted):
```
{"action": "open_file", "path": "/app/data/user.csv", "confidence": 0.97}

\u0000\u0000\u0001
```

mike: is this happening for synchronous calls only or also with the async streaming endpoint?

julian: streaming endpoint. sync (no-stream) looks clean. if we force batch_size=1 it's clean too.

anika: can we repro locally with the canary runner? what's the canary config?

julian: canary: model=zeta-2A:int8, profile=ptq-streaming, batching={min_tokens:1, max_batch:32}, kv_prefix_cache=on, stream=true. started at 2024-06-03 09:40 UTC.

sara: possible causes: kernel quant path producing extra bytes on streaming flush, or our streaming delimiter handling (we append sentinel after EOS and batching merges streams).

mike: also check the transformer decode buffer — if two streams concatenate in the same buffer and we trim by token count rather than byte offset, trailing leftover bytes could slip out.

julian: repro steps I used: run canary harness with 1000 streamed tool-invokes, payloads include various small json tool results. I see ~12 bad outputs. attaching minimal harness command:
```
./canary_runner --model zeta-2A:int8 --profile ptq-streaming --batching max=16 --streaming --samples 1000 --seed 42
```

anika: can you dump raw bytes for a few failing responses (hex)? that will tell if it's padding, nulls, or a mis-encoded token.

julian: dumped two failures: `7b 22 61 63 74 69 6f 6e 22 3a 20 22 6f 70 65 6e 5f 66 69 6c 65 22 2c 20 22 70 61 74 68 22 3a 20 22 2f 61 70 70 2f 64 61 74 61 2f 75 73 65 72 2e 63 73 76 22 2c 20 22 63 6f 6e 66 69 64 65 6e 63 65 22 3a 20 30 2e 39 37 7d 00 00 01` — looks like trailing nulls and one 0x01.

mike: that smells like zeroed padding from quantized kernel output plus a stale termination byte. can you repro with memory sanitizer on? maybe a small buffer write overshoot.

sara: also check our post-processing: we run a quick `strip_trailing_nonprintables()` on stream flush. maybe it only strips up to newline and leaves a control byte.

anika: for a quick mitigation can we add a strict JSON validator in the postprocess that drops any bytes after the first closing brace for JSON tool outputs? we can rate-limit it to canary and dedicated for now.

julian: good short-term plan. will PR a postprocess guard: findfirst('}') and truncate after that byte + sanity-check balanced braces.

mike: longer-term we should instrument the runtime: add per-request raw-byte dumps into canary logs (obfuscated) and a fast assertion that streaming buffer positions are reset after each produced sequence. add a metric for "postprocess-truncate" so we see how often mitigation kicks in.

sara: agree. also try to repro on float16 (no-quant) binary to confirm it's quant kernel specific. if float16 clean -> high prob quant kernel.

julian: ran quick float16 canary: no failures in 2000 samples. int8 still shows ~1.1%. opening issue and will push the guard PR tonight.

deploy-bot: Canary job zeta-2A-int8-streaming started (id: canary-78321) — view logs: https://ci.redwood.example/canary-78321

anika: thx. julian, tag me on the PR. we'll schedule a deeper kernel audit next week. :thumbsup:
